evidence.excerpt: Plasmid retention in a recombinant Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) strain carrying a pET-based expression vector was monitored over 40-hour fed-batch cultivations at three different specific growth rates (0.10, 0.20, and 0.35 h⁻¹) without antibiotic selection pressure. Samples were taken every four hours and plated on selective and non-selective media to calculate plasmid retention fraction. At µ = 0.10 h⁻¹, retention remained above 92% throughout; at µ = 0.35 h⁻¹, retention fell below 70% after 28 hours. Flow cytometry using a chromosomally integrated GFP marker confirmed plasmid-free segregant fractions independently of plating. Volumetric productivity of the target protein (a recombinant chitinase) tracked plasmid retention closely. A simple population balance model was parameterised to the data and predicts retention behaviour within ±8% across the growth rate range tested.
